PS2:the-fairly-oddparents-breakin-da-rul.d: The Fairly OddParents: Breakin' Da Rules is a video game released for the Game Boy Advance, GameCube, PlayStation 2, Xbox, and Windows in North America on November 10, 2003. It is based on the Nickelodeon cartoon The Fairly OddParents. It was developed by Blitz Games for the PlayStation 2, GameCube and Xbox, Helixe for Game Boy Advance and Gorilla for Windows, and published by THQ. Its sequel, The Fairly OddParents: Shadow Showdown, was released on the same platforms, except for the Xbox.

PC:star-trek-starfleet-academy.d: Star Trek: Starfleet Academy is a Star Trek PC simulation game developed and published by Interplay in 1997. The game simulates the life of a typical Starfleet cadet, with the player learning the basics of flying a starship and engaging in roleplaying with a crew of cadets, with the eventual goal of becoming captain of their own ship. The game included full motion video featuring William Shatner, Walter Koenig, and George Takei reprising their roles from the original television series and movies, and a multiplayer simulation mode allowing for up to 32 players. A tie-in novelization by Diane Carey was released by Pocket Books in June 1997.

Linux:majesty-fantasy-kingdom-sim.d: Majesty: The Fantasy Kingdom Sim is a real-time strategy (RTS) video game developed by Cyberlore Studios, and published by Hasbro Interactive under the MicroProse brand name for Windows in March 2000. It removes a central feature of the RTS genre, direct control over units. The game is not a simulator. That part of the title is a reference to Majesty's central joke: affectionate parodying of fantasy role-playing games (RPGs).

Linux:nethack.d: NetHack is a free roguelike video game developed by the NetHack Development Team (also known as the DevTeam), a group of developers who collaborate over the internet. It was first released on 28 July 1987 as a fork of Hack, which is itself based on Rogue, and it is one of the oldest video games still in active development. In the game, the player creates a character, then descends through the Mazes of Menace, a multi-level dungeon, fighting monsters and collecting treasure, with the goal of retrieving the Amulet of Yendor and escaping with it. NetHack has been cited as an influence on later games, including Diablo.
